title: Cap. IX Arg. 14 Sol close: election decree unknown a priori — elect cannot conclude they need not obey; no election-knowledge until they feel the study of obeying God
latin: Porro, cum electionis decretum sit hominibus a priori plane incognitum, et non nisi ex effectis et Spiritus testimonio ipsis electis revelatum, non modo falsum, sed a ratione et sensu communi alienum est, quod colligunt Arminiani, posse hosce electos concludere apud se nil opus esse ut soliciti sint de praestanda obedientia. Nam ipsi electi ne tenuissimam quidem suae electionis cognitionem habere possunt, priusquam sentiant in se hoc studium obediendi Deo, et vitam suam religiose transigendi: neque Spiritus Dei dignabitur hoc testimonium homini in caeno libidinum turpissimarum volutanti exhibere. Quomodo igitur concludet ex apprehensione electionis suae nil sibi opus esse sanctitate vitae, qui aliter colligere non potest se esse electum, quam ex effectis Spiritus sancti et sanctificantis?
pass_a: Further, since the decree of election is unto men a priori plainly unknown, and not revealed unto the elect themselves except from effects and the testimony of the Spirit, it is not only false, but alien from reason and common sense, what the Arminians gather — that these elect can conclude with themselves that there is no need that they be solicitous concerning rendering obedience. For the elect themselves cannot have even the slenderest knowledge of their election, before they feel in themselves this study of obeying God, and of passing their life religiously: nor will the Spirit of God deign to exhibit this testimony unto a man wallowing in the mire of most foul lusts. How therefore will he conclude from the apprehension of his election that there is no need unto him of holiness of life, who otherwise cannot gather that he is elect, than from the effects of the Holy and sanctifying Spirit?
pass_b: Further: the election decree is plainly unknown to men a priori, and is revealed to the elect themselves only from effects and the Spirit's testimony. So what the Arminians gather — that these elect can conclude they need not be solicitous about rendering obedience — is not only false, but alien to reason and common sense. The elect themselves cannot have even the slenderest knowledge of their election before they feel in themselves this study of obeying God and living religiously. Nor will God's Spirit deign to give that testimony to a man wallowing in the mire of foulest lusts. How then will he conclude from apprehending his election that he needs no holiness of life — when he can gather he is elect no other way than from the effects of the Holy and sanctifying Spirit?

lemmas.gloss: election unknown a priori; known from effects/Spirit

title: Cap. IX Arg. 14 Sol close: elect praxis — saints more studious of piety the more certain of election (patriarchs, Mary, apostles; 1 John iii. 3); profane presume and grow less careful, pious burn hotter
latin: Denique reclamat Arminio omnium sanctorum praxis, quos certum est eo studiosiores fuisse pietatis et verae obedientiae, quo certiores fuerunt suae electionis et vitae aeternae. Exemplo esse possunt sancti Patriarchae, Abrahamus, Isaacus, Jacobus, Beatissima mulierum Mater Domini nostri Jesu Christi, Petrus, Paulus, reliquique Apostoli: Imo omnis qui habet hanc spem in seipso, sanctificat se, sicut ille sanctus est, 1 Joann. iii. 3. Profani igitur homines, qui stulte praesumere solent, et otiose garrire de sua praedestinatione, inde redduntur de Deo colendo minus soliciti: sed piorum pectora, qui vivide sentiunt hoc beneficium ad se pertinere, inde incenduntur incredibili amore Dei et ardentissimo studio pietatis. Sic Bernardus, Epist. 107. Justus quis est nisi qui amanti se Deo vicem rependit amoris? Quod non fit, nisi revelante Spiritu per fidem, homini aeternum Dei propositum super sua salute futura.
pass_a: Finally the praxis of all the saints cries out against Arminius, whom it is certain were so much the more studious of piety and of true obedience, the more certain they were of their election and of everlasting life. Example can be the holy Patriarchs, Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, the most Blessed of women the Mother of our Lord Jesus Christ, Peter, Paul, and the remaining Apostles: Nay every one who has this hope in himself sanctifies himself, even as he is holy, 1 Joann. iii. 3. Profane men therefore, who are wont foolishly to presume, and idly to chatter of their predestination, are thence rendered less solicitous concerning worshipping God: but the breasts of the pious, who vividly feel that this benefit pertains unto them, are thence kindled with incredible love of God and most ardent study of piety. So Bernard, Epist. 107. Who is just except he who repays love unto God loving him? Which is not done, except the Spirit revealing through faith unto a man the everlasting purpose of God concerning his future salvation.
pass_b: Finally the praxis of all the saints cries out against Arminius. It is certain they were the more studious of piety and true obedience, the more certain they were of their election and everlasting life. Example: the holy Patriarchs Abraham, Isaac, Jacob; the most Blessed of women, the Mother of our Lord Jesus Christ; Peter, Paul, and the other Apostles. Nay, everyone who has this hope in himself sanctifies himself, as he is holy (1 John iii. 3). So profane men, who foolishly presume and idly chatter of their predestination, grow less careful about worshipping God. But pious hearts, who vividly feel this benefit belongs to them, are kindled with incredible love of God and most ardent study of piety. So Bernard (Epist. 107): Who is just but he who repays love to God who loves him? That is not done unless the Spirit reveals through faith to a man God's eternal purpose concerning his future salvation.

lemmas.gloss: more certain of election → more studious of piety
Bernard: just love answers revealed purpose

title: Cap. IX Arg. 14 Sol close: reprobation half — no one appointed to damnation except from gaze on preceding sin (original, actual, or both); God hates none unto damnation without considering sin
latin: Hactenus de praedestinatione dictum est: Jam ad eam partem objectionis quae reprobationem spectat veniamus; Cui respondemus breviter, Neminem ex nostra sententia ad damnationem deputatum esse nisi ex intuitu praecedentis peccati, originalis nempe, actualis, aut utriusque. Neminem enim Deus odit ad damnationem absque consideratione peccati; Nec magis odit homines quam peccatum, quos nunquam ita odisset nisi propter peccatum.
pass_a: Thus far has it been spoken of predestination: Now let us come unto that part of the objection which looks unto reprobation; Unto which we answer briefly, that no one from our sentence is appointed unto damnation except from the intuit of preceding sin, namely original, actual, or of both. For God hates no one unto damnation without consideration of sin; Nor does he hate men more than sin, whom he would never so have hated except on account of sin.
pass_b: Thus far of predestination. Now to that part of the objection which looks to reprobation. We answer briefly: on our view no one is appointed to damnation except from a gaze on preceding sin — original, actual, or both. For God hates no one unto damnation without considering sin. Nor does he hate men more than sin — he would never have hated them so except because of sin.

lemmas.gloss: damnation only with gaze on preceding sin

lemmas.lemma: nunquam ita odisset nisi propter peccatum
lemmas.gloss: hate unto damnation only because of sin

title: Cap. IX Arg. 14 Sol close: our reprobation doctrine drives no one to despair who studies to avoid sin and obey — that study is surest election-mark; those not yet feeling it must use granted means, not despair
latin: Nemo denique mortalium est quem nostra sententia de reprobatione ad desperationem potest adigere, si studeat vitare peccatum et Deo obedire; quia hoc ipsum studium est nostro judicio certissimum electionis argumentum. Nec debent desperare, qui nondum sentiunt tale studium, sed iis mediis uti, quae sunt illis a Deo concessa, haud dubitantes quin Deus sic agentibus suam misericordiam sit exhibiturus.
pass_a: Finally there is no one of mortals whom our sentence concerning reprobation can drive unto despair, if he study to avoid sin and to obey God; because this very study is in our judgment the most certain argument of election. Nor ought they to despair who do not yet feel such a study, but to use those media which have been granted them by God, by no means doubting but that God will exhibit his mercy unto those so acting.
pass_b: Finally: our doctrine of reprobation can drive no mortal to despair if he studies to avoid sin and obey God — for that very study is in our judgment the surest mark of election. Nor should those despair who do not yet feel such a study. They should use the means God has granted them, not doubting that God will show his mercy to those who so act.

lemmas.gloss: not yet feeling it: use means, do not despair

title: Cap. X open: our sentence on reprobation is set forth and confirmed — after weighing adversaries, what our view is and on what stays it rests
latin: CAP. X. Nostra de Reprobatione sententia exponitur et confirmatur. Hactenus Adversariorum sententiam et argumenta expendimus. Jam quae sit nostra de reprobatione sententia, quibusque firmamentis nitatur, videamus.
pass_a: CHAPTER X. Our sentence concerning Reprobation is set forth and confirmed. Thus far we have weighed the sentence and arguments of the Adversaries. Now let us see what our sentence concerning reprobation is, and upon what stays it rests.
pass_b: CHAPTER X. Our sentence on Reprobation is set forth and confirmed. Thus far we have weighed the adversaries' view and arguments. Now let us see what our view of reprobation is, and on what stays it rests.

lemmas.gloss: Cap. X: state and confirm our reprobation doctrine

title: Cap. X: to avoid calumny — our Church rejects both those who make God cause of unbelief/damnation by absolute antecedent will, and Arminian/Pelagian errors that make each man after common sufficient grace the smith of his own eternal fortune
latin: Atque hic, ut vitemus malevolorum calumnias, subinde cogimur repetere, Ecclesiam nostram non minus rejicere portentosas illorum opiniones, qui sic reprobationis decretum nobis depingunt, ut Deum infidelitatis et impoenitentiae humanae causam statuant, ipsamque adeo perditionem et damnationem hominum in Dei absolutam et antecedentem voluntatem revocent, quam Arminianorum ex Pelagii faecibus haustos errores, qui sic praedestinationis et reprobationis decreta nobis proponunt, ut interim unumquemque, post decretum de administranda communiter gratia sufficiente, constituant in gratuitis et aeternis bonis fabrum fortunae suae; Deo scilicet praestolante et intuente quid homines sint facturi, et prout praeviderit eos credituros, aut non credituros, eligente eos vel non eligente, hoc est, reprobante.
pass_a: And here, that we may avoid the calumnies of the malevolent, we are again and again compelled to repeat, that our Church no less rejects the portentous opinions of those who so depict unto us the decree of reprobation that they establish God as the cause of human unbelief and impenitence, and even recall the very perdition and damnation of men unto the absolute and antecedent will of God, than the errors of the Arminians drawn from the dregs of Pelagius, who so propose unto us the decrees of predestination and of reprobation that meanwhile they constitute every one, after the decree concerning administering sufficient grace commonly, as smith of his own fortune in gratuitous and everlasting goods; God namely waiting and looking what men will do, and according as he shall have foreseen them about to believe, or not about to believe, electing them or not electing, that is, reprobating.
pass_b: And here, to avoid malevolent calumnies, we must keep repeating: our Church rejects no less those portentous opinions that so paint the reprobation decree as to make God the cause of human unbelief and impenitence, and even refer men's very perdition and damnation to God's absolute antecedent will — than the Arminian errors drawn from Pelagius's dregs, which so set the decrees of predestination and reprobation that after the decree to administer common sufficient grace, each man is made smith of his own fortune in free and everlasting goods. God waits and watches what men will do, and as he foresaw them about to believe or not, elects them or does not elect — that is, reprobates.

lemmas.gloss: reject Arminian each-man-smith of eternal fortune

title: Cap. X: human will leading divine will is neither worthy of God nor of Scripture — predestination is preparation of efficacious grace and glory from mere mercy, not election from foreseen faith
latin: Hanc praedestinationem et reprobationem, in qua humana voluntas ducit Divinam, nec Deo dignam putamus, nec sacris literis consentaneam. E contra igitur, sicuti monstravimus, Praedestinationem non esse singularium personarum ex praevisa illarum fide et perseverantia electionem ad vitam aeternam, sed praeparationem gratiae efficacis certis quibusdam personis ex mera Dei misericordia, et praeparationem gloriae sempiternae iisdem ex eadem misericordia.
pass_a: This predestination and reprobation, in which the human will leads the Divine, we judge neither worthy of God, nor agreeable unto the sacred letters. On the contrary therefore, as we have shown, Predestination is not the election of singular persons unto everlasting life from their foreseen faith and perseverance, but the preparation of efficacious grace for certain persons from the mere mercy of God, and the preparation of everlasting glory for the same from the same mercy.
pass_b: We judge that scheme — predestination and reprobation in which human will leads the divine — neither worthy of God nor agreeable to Scripture. On the contrary side, as we have shown, Predestination is something else. It is not election of singular persons to everlasting life from their foreseen faith and perseverance. It is God's mere-mercy preparation of efficacious grace for certain persons, and of everlasting glory for them from that same mercy.

lemmas.gloss: predestination = prepared grace and glory from mercy

title: Cap. X: non-election / negative reprobation defined — not pre-damnation from foreseen final unbelief, but denial from mere will of the special mercy that softens and leads to life (Bradwardine; Rom. ix. 16, 18)
latin: Ita dicimus, Non-electionem, praeteritionem sive reprobationem negativam haud esse singularium personarum ex praevisa finali earundem infidelitate et impoenitentia praedamnationem, (quamvis tale decretum agnoscamus) sed ex mera Dei voluntate denegationem ejus specialis misericordiae, quae infidelitatem et impoenitentiam tollit emolliendo, et ad vitam aeternam perducit in fide et sanctitate stabiliendo et conservando. Vel brevius ex Bradwardino nostro, qui profundi Doctoris cognomentum sibi meruit, Praedestinatio est aeterna praeparatio a voluntate Divina gratiae finalis in via, et beatitudinis aeternae in patria, creaturis quibusdam rationalibus, lib. 1. cap. 45. pag. 421. Et reprobatio est aeterna Dei nolitio conferendi talia in quibusdam personis, Ibid. pag. 426. Cum Apostolo defendimus hanc electionem non esse volentis, neque currentis, sed miserentis Dei, Rom. ix. 16. et hanc non-electionem, reprobationem sive nolitionem aeternam non esse ortam ex praevisa infidelitate, aut impoenitentia hominum, sed ex mera ejus libertate, qui cujus vult miseretur, et quem vult indurat, Rom. ix. 18. Quod, interprete Augustino, perinde est ac si dixisset Apostolus, cujus vult miseretur, et cujus non vult non miseretur, De praedest. et grat. cap. 6.
pass_a: So we say that Non-election, preterition or negative reprobation is by no means the pre-damnation of singular persons from their foreseen final unbelief and impenitence, (although we acknowledge such a decree) but from the mere will of God the denial of that special mercy which takes away unbelief and impenitence by softening, and leads unto everlasting life by establishing and conserving in faith and holiness. Or more briefly from our Bradwardine, who merited unto himself the surname of the profound Doctor, Predestination is the everlasting preparation by the Divine will of final grace in the way, and of everlasting beatitude in the fatherland, for certain rational creatures, lib. 1. cap. 45. pag. 421. And reprobation is the everlasting nilling of God of conferring such things in certain persons, Ibid. pag. 426. With the Apostle we defend that this election is not of him that wills, nor of him that runs, but of God that shows mercy, Rom. ix. 16. and that this non-election, reprobation or everlasting nilling did not arise from foreseen unbelief, or impenitence of men, but from his mere liberty, who has mercy on whom he wills, and whom he wills he hardens, Rom. ix. 18. Which, Augustine interpreting, is as if the Apostle had said, on whom he wills he has mercy, and on whom he wills not he has not mercy, De praedest. et grat. cap. 6.
pass_b: So we put it this way. Non-election — preterition, negative reprobation — is not pre-damnation of singular persons from foreseen final unbelief and impenitence. (We do acknowledge a decree of that kind.) What it is, from God's mere will, is denial of that special mercy which softens away unbelief and impenitence, and which leads to everlasting life by fixing and keeping a person in faith and holiness. Bradwardine, our profound Doctor, says it shorter: Predestination is the eternal preparation by divine will of final grace in the way, and of eternal beatitude in the fatherland, for certain rational creatures (lib. 1. cap. 45. pag. 421). Reprobation is God's eternal nilling to confer such things in certain persons (Ibid. pag. 426). With the Apostle we hold that this election is not of him who wills, nor of him who runs, but of God who shows mercy (Rom. ix. 16). And this non-election — this reprobation or eternal nilling — did not spring from men's foreseen unbelief or impenitence. It sprang from his mere liberty: who has mercy on whom he wills, and whom he wills he hardens (Rom. ix. 18). Augustine's reading is as if the Apostle had said: on whom he wills he has mercy, and on whom he wills not he has not mercy (De praedest. et grat. cap. 6).

lemmas.gloss: negative reprobation = deny special softening mercy
Bradwardine defs; election/reprobation from mere liberty
